# Quantiiv-Engine — repository router

One uv workspace (`uv.lock`, `.venv`) contains ROGER v4 (`roger/`), Switchyard (`agents/`),
Agent Capabilities (`capabilities/`), Analysis Studio (`studio/`), Quantiiv Console (`console/`),
Data Engine (`data/`), the Email
Router (`email-router/`), the Standalone Pricing System (`pricing/`), jobs (`jobs/`), libraries
(`libs/`), dev tooling (`devtools/`), and Quantiiv API v2 (`api/`).

Scoped `AGENTS.md` files are cumulative. Read this file, then every nearer router. Keep facts
at the narrowest scope. `CLAUDE.md` symlinks to `AGENTS.md`; edit `AGENTS.md` only.

## Authority and routes

- `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` indexes the repo-wide rules layer. Each named rule document governs its
  surface. A member may add local rules but cannot contradict that surface authority.
- Otherwise the nearest member `AGENTS.md` governs its subtree. Read it before editing there.
- Inside `data/**` only, authority is ratified constitution > statutes
  (`data/docs/CONVENTIONS.md`, `data/docs/canonical/*`) > `data/AGENTS.md`. `CONST-*` articles reach
  nothing outside that subtree.
- Joe's direction overrides repository prose. README files are orientation, not authority.

| Work | Read / run |
|---|---|
| a change to what a system does — new behavior, changed behavior, a contract that moves | `feature-development` skill; its authority is `docs/spec-conventions.md`. Write the packet before the code |
| reviewing a PR or work branch before it merges | `qe-pr-review` skill |
| executing a ratified packet — stages, briefs, delegation, review | `docs/implementation-flow.md` |
| contribution rules, one-effort/one-PR, draft-default CI, worktrees | `docs/development.md` |
| tracking work in Linear: issues, observations, state moves, owed applies | `linear-ops` skill |
| **before you comment on a GitHub PR, a GitHub issue, or a Linear issue** | `docs/development.md` § "Watermark every agent comment on GitHub and Linear" — writing as a person starts with `[AGENT]`; Bibi is exempt |
| canonical product, domain, system, API, layer, and component names | `repo-domain-glossary` skill |
| workspace setup, GAR, sync, lock, dependencies | `docs/uv-workspace.md` |
| CI/deploy/previews/releases/baselines/secrets | `docs/ci.md` |
| promoting development to production | `prod-promotion` skill |
| **before reading any CI result or watching a PR** | `ci-ops` skill — use the repository observer for every status read and watch, including post-merge trunk verification |
| tools, callables, skills, equipment loadouts | `docs/capabilities-authoring.md` |
| document placement | `docs/doc-conventions.md` |
| writing or revising text a person reads — no gate checks it | `language-standard` skill; skip for code-only work |
| signature-change and failure-set triage | `docs/development-triage.md` |
| Data Engine | `data/AGENTS.md`, then `data/constitution/INDEX.md` |
| Quantiiv API v2 (auth authority, intended single ingress) | `api/AGENTS.md` |
| Quantiiv Console, standalone npm dashboard | `console/AGENTS.md` |
| Standalone Pricing System | `pricing/AGENTS.md`, then `docs/specs/2026/2026-08-15-pricing-monorepo-fold/` |

Member routers name the skills and tools scoped to their own subtree.

## Repository invariants

- Use `docs/canonical/seam-fidelity.md`. Fake dependencies at the wire/emulator, not
  at a decision seam, and inject a fault. Do not add vocabulary or string/file-absence tests where
  a one-time grep suffices; retain behavioral guards, fail-closed checks, and goldens.
- Where a member publishes `docs/canonical/test-fidelity.md`, that charter is authoritative inside
  it; open it before the doctrine. Elsewhere the doctrine applies directly.
- Resolve tests and fixtures inside this repository; never depend on a sibling checkout or its venv.
- Tests run in parallel and set up once: `docs/canonical/test-efficiency.md` binds.
- `uv.lock` is the only Python dependency surface; never restore `requirements.txt` or the retired
  `roger-dev` service.
- Reach Google through the raw `google.cloud` SDKs (`firestore`, `storage`, `secretmanager`,
  `tasks_v2`, `run_v2`); keep `quantiiv.cloud.*` and `quantiiv_skills` at zero when copying donor code.
- QE owns ROGER v4, Studio, and Data services end to end. ROGER v3 and Agent Gateway live
  elsewhere. Terraform owns Cloud Run configuration; direct gcloud configuration is drift
  (`docs/ci.md` § Who changes deployed resources).
- Identity is global and capability is resource-scoped. Split credentials by environment only when
  they protect environment-distinct resources (`data/docs/CONVENTIONS.md` § Auth scoping).
- Golden/snapshot regenerations are separate reviewed commits using their member's sanctioned
  generator. Do not hand-edit generated artifacts.
- A new generated artifact or writer owes a `.merge-batcher.toml` tier-1 stanza or
  exemption in its PR; the gate sees only declared generators and banners (`docs/ci.md`).
- Before committing a fold of `origin/development` into a stacked lane, verify
  `git diff origin/development` is exactly the lane's intentional changes: a squash merge lets an
  old merge-base keep the wrong side, and git resolves WRONGLY WITHOUT A CONFLICT when two lanes
  edit one literal to the same value and the truth is now the next one along. Re-derive such a
  value from its source after any fold; never read it.
- **Then IMPORT the folded tree:** trunk deleting a package your lane only imports merges clean
  and the diff check cannot see it. `make fold` runs that import (`make bake`) before it commits.
- A signature change owes `git merge-tree` before it merges: trunk can land a caller at the old
  signature that git merges clean. See `docs/development-triage.md`.
- Open every PR as a draft: it runs repository contracts only, and its `ci-verdict` is red by
  design. The `preview` and `ci:full` labels buy back a preview stack or the suite gate,
  independently; only `preview` deploys one, for visual or deployed checks. Ready spends the
  full gate, after a green `make verify-changed`. `docs/development.md` § Draft is the cheap default.

## Setup and tests

Cold-start every worktree before trusting results (sandboxes: `docs/cloud-env.md`):

```bash
gcloud auth login --update-adc   # once per machine; covers private GAR packages
make lane SLUG=<slug>            # or `make bootstrap`
```

Each member's `AGENTS.md` carries its own test command, parallelism, and marker set; run the suite
from the member you changed. `.github/ci/python-tests.yml` is the authoritative lane/marker set, and CI
is the baseline authority. Two traps a member command will not warn you about: a marker-gated seam
can collect zero silently, so run its whole module when you change one; and a lane without
`addopts` runs live tests unless you pass the member's exclusion marker, which calls the production
Quantiiv API.

Run `make verify-changed` before pushing behavior changes. Follow `docs/development.md` § Local
behavior before CI for test depth and reporting; this local plan is not CI-equivalent.

Triage red suites before changing product code; a bare count is not a gate. Recipe:
`docs/development-triage.md`.

## Where context goes

Keep only durable rules that still change a decision in three months. Put architecture/design in
`docs/specs/<slug>/`, CI mechanics in `docs/ci.md`, scoped rules in the member router, focused
procedures in an owning runbook, and incidents/run state in the PR, spec ledger, or `STATE.md`.
Update stale instructions in the same change. Keep this file at or below 10 KiB.

# Reviewing a Quantiiv-Engine PR

A monorepo review answers one question a single-repo review never has to: **did the change
move every consumer it owns?** QE holds the producer and its consumers in one tree, so there
is no "the other repo will catch up" — a contract that moved without its consumers is a
regression that ships, and a cutover is always possible in the same PR. One consumer is the
exception: the production image on shared State (L1.8) never moves in the PR.

Verdict-oriented, not finding-count-oriented. A confident wrong finding costs more than a
missed nit: it sends the author to fix code that was already right.

## Scope the candidate before reviewing it

```bash
cd <lane>                                       # never review from the trunk checkout
BASE=$(git merge-base origin/development HEAD)  # merge-base, NOT trunk tip
git diff --stat "$BASE"...HEAD
BASE="$BASE" JSON=1 make impact                 # changed paths + the CI surfaces they activate
```

Then read, yourself, before delegating anything:

- **Packet contracts first.** Read `contracts/` before other packet files. Treat each consumer table as the L1 starting point.

- **The spec, if one is named.** `docs/specs/<slug>/` in the repo, or the member's spec dir.
  Never delegate interpretation of the source of truth — a lane that infers intent from the
  diff will always find the diff intentional.
- **The PR body.** "Intentionally unchanged", "Compatibility impact", and the change-discipline
  checkboxes are the author's *claimed* scope. The diff is the *actual* scope. Where they
  disagree is a finding before any lens runs.
- **The `ci-ops` skill, before reading any mutable CI or PR state.** Then use `docs/ci.md`
  to interpret the snapshot. See L6.
- **The [design-system skill](../design-system/SKILL.md#reviewing-proposed-and-implemented-ui),
  when the candidate changes application UI or its data/state behavior.** Apply its
  implemented-UI review across L3, L4, L5, and L6. Include the skill and relevant
  reference paths in each UI review brief; delegated reviewers read them themselves.
  This includes API loading, cache use, and task lifetime changes without a visual diff.
  The design lint already enforces the rules in its `references/enforced-rules.md`; review
  what it cannot check, each new `shadcn/*` suppression's reason, and any growth in
  `studio/eslint-suppressions.json`, which may only shrink.
  Report and deck contents use their own authoring guidance.

## The nine lenses

Each lens is a bounded job with its own evidence bar. Run them concurrently; each returns
findings in the report format below, or `none`.

### L1 — Cross-consumer cutover

*Did every in-repo consumer of a contract this PR moved, move with it?*

Classify each changed file:

| Role | Where |
|---|---|
| Contract source | `data/src/qde/**`, `data/src/qwire/**`, `roger/contracts/**`, `libs/quantiiv-access/**`, `libs/quantiiv-common/**`, `api/**` routes |
| Generated mirror | `data/docs/openapi.json`, `data/docs/openapi.json`, `data/clients/metrics-typescript/src/generated/**`, `roger/clients/roger-typescript/src/generated/**`, `roger/contracts/generated/**` |
| Consumer | `studio/apps/studio/**` (`@quantiiv/metrics-client`, `@quantiiv/state-client`, `@quantiiv/roger-client`), `capabilities/quantiiv-tools/**` (`quantiiv_metrics_client`, `quantiiv_state_client`), `roger/**` |

1. **Source moved, mirror didn't** → either the change is not wire-visible (make the author
   prove it) or the generator was not run. Verify, don't assume:
   ```bash
   make -C data openapi-check                                    # OpenAPI baseline drift
   pnpm --filter @quantiiv/metrics-client contracts:check         # metrics.gen.ts freshness
   pnpm --filter @quantiiv/roger-client contracts:check           # ROGER mirrors
   cd roger && ../.venv/bin/python contracts/generated/emit_sources.py --check
   ```
   Never hand-resolve a conflict in a generated file — regenerate from its authority
   (`make -C data regen-openapi`, then the client's `generate`), in its own commit.

2. **For every field, status code, or enum value added, removed, or repurposed**, grep every
   consumer by name — the symbol *and* any string it appears in. Do not stop at the import.

3. **Compile-clean is not cutover.** The loudest failure in this repo's history: the engine
   moved `result_too_large` from a 200-plus-notice to a 413. Studio still typechecked, because
   it never named the status code — it branched on the notice and re-served the rows from the
   export door, parsing `actual=N, limit=M` out of the detail string. The 413 threw before
   either path ran, killing the notice *and* the fallback. For each moved value ask:

   - does any consumer **branch** on it, or on its absence?
   - does any consumer **parse it out of prose** — a detail string, a label, a filename?
   - does any consumer **key state** on it, or use it to choose a fallback path?

4. **The reverse drift.** A consumer half that changed alone is the same defect from the other
   side. When producer and consumer are one contract, they land together — prove it:
   ```bash
   git log -S'<token>' --oneline -- data studio     # did both halves ever land in one commit?
   ```
   If they did once and this PR changes only one, the PR is reverting a cross-repo contract.

5. **ROGER is becoming a consumer of the Data Engine contracts.** Treat `roger/**` as a live
   consumer surface, not a future one; `quantiiv-metrics-client` is already in its dependencies.

6. **Some consumers are not in this tree, and those get the opposite verdict.** `quantiiv-api`
   owns the access contract and the config-plane writer; QE carries committed *mirrors* of them
   — `tools/access-contract/` byte-diffs against a sha256-pinned upstream image
   (`tools/access-contract/UPSTREAM_IMAGE`), and `data/tests/unit/_config_plane_ts_mirror.js`
   replays a transcription of that writer against the shipped identity vectors in
   `_config_plane_vectors.json`. In-repo cutover is impossible here. So for a mirrored contract
   the requirements invert: **the mirror and its vectors must move in this PR**, and the
   cross-repo landing order must be named in the PR body. That is the one legitimate reason
   `docs/development.md` allows a split — but it has to be *stated*, not inferred by the
   reviewer. A new family or field added on the QE side with an untouched mirror is a P1
   whether or not CI is green, because the mirror gate only proves the *committed* mirror
   matches upstream, not that it covers what you added.

7. **A metric's text is part of its contract.** Studio's definition dialog and ROGER's company
   facts read a metric's description, methodology and formula. A PR that adds or changes a
   public metric or calculation kind answers the review checklist in
   `data/src/qde/metrics/catalog/AGENTS.md` § Describing a metric; an unanswered item is a
   finding.

8. **The production image is a consumer of every State migration and stored-envelope version.**
   A merge to `development` applies the PR's migrations to `quantiiv_state_prod` minutes later,
   while production serves that plane on the `production` branch's code until the next release.
   For every function body, CHECK, DEFAULT, trigger, policy, grant and version literal the PR's
   migrations change, find what production sends and reads with
   `git grep -n '<name or literal>' origin/production -- data jobs`, and check that the migrated
   door still accepts it and still stamps it the way production's readers expect. A migration
   that swaps an accepted literal instead of adding one, or moves a DEFAULT production relies
   on, is a P0 whatever CI says. The PR's seams run new code against the new schema and cannot
   see it. Ask for the production-tip seam run the rule requires
   ([rule](../../../data/docs/CONVENTIONS.md#production-runs-your-migration-before-it-runs-your-code)). This covers every stored, versioned envelope: report evidence,
   metrics and report envelopes, export layouts and formats, notification and email payloads,
   and every `stored_documents` kind.

9. **Studio is the editor of every report envelope the store admits.** A PR that changes the
   envelope wire, Studio's report reader, save writer or run request, or the store's
   `data/src/qde/reports/alignment_profile.py` keeps `make -C data studio-report-contract`
   green. `report_contract_worklist.py` must be empty unless the PR states a split naming each
   entry's owner. A shape the store admits and Studio cannot open, save unchanged or run is a
   finding. Fix it in Studio or refuse it in the profile; a read-only carve-out does not count.

A blocking L1 finding names the consumer at `file:line`, the value or shape it reads, and what
it does when the new shape arrives.

### L2 — Dual authority

*Does this already exist, and if so, what justifies a second one?*

One type, one function, one home. For each new exported symbol, endpoint, model, or helper,
search for a near-duplicate **by intent, not by name** — the duplicate is rarely named alike.

Specific QE shapes, loudest first:

- **A hand-written TS interface whose fields mirror a generated schema.** If a surface in
  `studio/apps/studio/**` declares its own shape for something `metrics.gen.ts` or
  `@quantiiv/roger-client` already publishes, the generated client is no longer the source of truth for
  that surface, and the next contract change will pass CI and break at runtime.
- **A Python model mirroring one in `core.contracts`** — or in the client package that already
  wraps it.
- **Two call sites doing the same derivation** — redaction, normalization, formatting, scope
  narrowing. Two homes means one gets fixed. Collapse to one shared function.
- **A bespoke helper beside a canonical one** in `libs/`.

The bar for a new one: *name the existing thing, state precisely what it cannot do, and say why
extending it is worse than duplicating it.* "It's a different layer" counts only when the layers
have genuinely different authority — `[tool.importlinter]` in the root `pyproject.toml` is the
authority on which boundaries are real, not intuition. If the new boundary is real and worth
keeping, ask whether it should have an import-linter contract of its own.

### L3 — Seam fidelity

*Do the tests prove the new behavior, or the retired one?*

Doctrine lives in `docs/canonical/seam-fidelity.md` and the member
charters — `roger/docs/canonical/test-fidelity.md`, and the equivalents in `agents/` and `data/`.
Read the charter for the member you're reviewing. QE-specific checks:

- **A moved identity leaves stale fakes behind.** When a PR changes a join key, identity, or
  lookup, check whether the wire-fake still matches the *old* one. This has shipped: a change
  that replaced a `load_source + location` join with `raw_location_id` left the BigQuery
  wire-fake matching on the retired pair — so every attribution seam was proving the join the
  PR deleted, and the new join had no coverage at all while CI was green.
- **Fixtures must be directional.** A fixture that passes under both the old and new behavior
  proves nothing. The one that closed the case above gave all three fact rows the *identical*
  display name, so the retired registration could only be excluded by its id.
- **RED-verify every fix.** Revert the fix, confirm that exact test fails with the exact wrong
  value, restore. An author who cannot state the red output did not run it. In the report, name
  both values — `0.8333… vs 0` is evidence; "added a test" is not.
- **A repointed test that runs a different path than its assertion.** Repointing a click or a
  call at the new door is not enough if the scenario never *opens* that door — the test then
  passes against a path the assertion was never about.
- **Assertions on proxies.** A test (or the product code) reading a filename, a label, a copy
  string, or `length >= LIMIT` instead of the state itself. Same defect class as L1.3, and it
  breaks on the next reword. If the door publishes its own signal, read the signal.
- **Fault injection.** A boundary that changed with no injected fault is unproven.
- **Inventory every fake.** Search for mocks, fakes, monkeypatches, scripted models, in-memory stores, skips, and emulator lanes.
- **Classify each fake.** Record its current seam, faithful seam, and the bug class the faithful seam catches.
- **Check cross-service joins.** Determine whether any suite drives the real upstream runtime.
- **Stop on an absent seam.** Require the repository to build the faithful seam before further audit.
- Not a finding: absent vocabulary tests, string-absence gates, or migration lock-ins. A
  one-time grep proves those at zero maintenance cost; their absence is correct.

### L4 — Intent and scope fidelity

*Is the diff what the spec asked for — no less, and no more?*

- **Trace every hunk to a stated intent.** A change that is defensible but unasked-for is still
  a scope finding, especially when it alters existing behavior. Ask whether it belongs to this
  effort or is a second one.
- **Non-goals.** A spec that declares something out of scope, and a diff that does it anyway,
  is a contradiction the author must resolve — not the reviewer.
- **Confounded evidence.** When two independent changes ship together, neither one's evidence
  is interpretable on its own. A PR claiming "every KPI matches legacy to the cent" while
  changing both the join *and* the evidence model has measured their sum. Ask which change the
  evidence isolates. This is non-blocking on code and blocking on the claim.
- **Bridge scaffolding is a scope failure, not a phasing choice.** `docs/development.md` bans
  dual paths, re-export stubs, flag-gated A/B, and "delete the old path later" between phases
  of one effort. Retiring a path is a clean cutover in the same change: move the meaningful
  assertions onto the new single source of truth, then delete the old path and its tests.
  The exception is shared State: accepting the literal production still writes is required,
  not scaffolding (L1.8), and its removal is a later migration after the release.
- **One effort, one PR.** Eight worktrees is still one PR. A split is legitimate only for a
  stated external constraint named in the PR body — a cross-repo landing order, a live consumer
  that cannot move. "Built in separate lanes" and "easier to review" are not constraints.

### L5 — Structure

Architectural smells. For depth, `thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review` is the harsher pass and
should be run instead of restating it here. What this lens owns in QE:

- Feature logic leaking into `libs/`, or logic landing in the wrong deployable. `core` imports
  no deployable; `metrics` and `state` never import each other. Those are enforced contracts —
  a change that wants to cross one is an architecture question, not a lint failure.
- A file the PR pushes past ~1000 lines.
- New ad-hoc branching bolted into an unrelated flow, where the cleaner move deletes the branch
  rather than centralizing it.
- Fix placement: a guard belongs at the single point every path resolves through, not at one
  entry point. Clamping in the input handler leaves typed dates, restored saved views, and URL
  state uncovered; clamping in the resolver covers all of them.

### L6 — Evidence integrity

*Is green actually green?*

Read the `ci-ops` skill and `docs/ci.md` before interpreting any result. Acquire mutable PR state
through the repository observer, not a separately timed PR or check query:

```bash
python3 tools/ci/ci_ops.py status <pr> --json
```

Then:

- **Read required contexts from the observer's effective-rules snapshot.** `ci-verdict` is the
  current code gate and fails closed. A red advisory lane beside a green required set still needs
  triage; a green lane beside a red required context is not a pass.
- **Rung 3.** Add `preview` when a change needs deployed or visual verification, such as a Studio UI change. The user may add it too. Ready for review does not request a preview. If no behavior needs deployed verification, explain why Rung 3 is not applicable; no preview is required. For each behavior with a deployed surface, require a preview declaration with the published URL, head SHA, and observable. A bare `N/A` is incomplete, **and a declared head SHA that is not the head under review is stale, not evidence.** Dropping the `preview` label leaves the `pr-<N>` revision serving its last build for the life of the PR, so a reachable URL and a green observable no longer imply the code you are reading.
- **Which gates *ran* on this SHA — not which are green.** Producers are path-gated, so a job
  that never ran reads as green. This is how trunk carried a golden that did not match its own
  rendering for weeks: the `studio` job is gated on its own paths, so ROGER-only pushes never
  exercised it. No signal reads as green.
- **The right gate.** `make check-seams` is not `make seams` — the former also runs the
  docker-backed State DB and migration seams. A regression can look locally green purely
  because the cheaper target was run. The SDK wheel seams additionally need working GAR auth
  (`make doctor` checks it) or they ERROR on a 401 that reads like a code failure.
- **A fold-in invalidates every prior gate run.** If the lane merged trunk after its last green
  run, the merged tree has never been tested. A clean merge is not evidence.
- **Triage before blaming the diff.** Compare failing node-id sets and classify each as
  contention, pre-existing baseline, or regression. A bare pass count is not a gate; CI is the
  baseline authority.
- **Generated artifacts.** Everything generated must come from its sanctioned generator — a
  hand-edited golden is a defeated gate. Commit shape then splits by artifact class, and getting
  it backwards is itself a finding:
  - *Goldens and snapshots* land in their own reviewed commit, separate from the behaviour
    change that moved them.
  - *The methodology bake* is the opposite: the source edit, `make bake` output, and the
    `roger/src/roger/config/models.py` digest pin must land **together in one commit**, because
    a tree whose pin does not match its bake fails at import. Splitting it is the defect.
- **A deferred-suite run** skipped every change-gated producer because the PR is a draft without
  the `ci:full` label, and can never merge. `ci-verdict` is red by design and the triage check says
  `suites deferred`; that is not a defect to triage or a run to re-run.
  Its green means almost nothing; do not read it as a pass.

### L7 — Load-sensitive test shape

*Will every changed test keep the same verdict under shard contention?*

Inspect every test the PR adds or changes for absolute wall-clock bounds, wall-clock attribution
floors, fixed-size pools or process limits under shard parallelism, unseeded random values compared
with an equality or vocabulary, timeouts used as speed assertions, and rendered durations inside
asserted strings (`"dispatch=0.00s" in output`, signal `duration_literal_assert`; one that echoes a
number the test configured is a message check, a rendered zero is always a bound). The mechanical
inventory is
`tools/ci/gate/test_shape_gate.py`; its live proof ledger is
`tools/ci/gate/load_sensitive_tests.toml`.

Demand a registry-enum shape, a comment stating the invariant and why contention cannot reverse it,
and a fault proof that fails when that invariant is broken. For a deadline window, check the two
named constants `T` and `S`, `S >= max(4 * T, T + 4.0)`, and the midpoint bound
`elapsed < (T + S) / 2` beside the typed outcome. A loosened number, retry marker, or skip is not
hardening and is a blocking finding.

### L8 — CI selection and cost

*Does each job this PR adds or re-triggers run only when the change can break what it proves?*

When the diff adds or splits a job, or changes a paths filter, a selector table, a matrix,
`runs-on`, or a partition rule, read the PR's selection cost: job-hours per 80 PRs, before and
after (`docs/ci.md` § Failure baselines and test selection). Each new trigger path outside what the
job's tests import, execute or read needs a reason. A trigger wider than that reach (`.github/**`,
`tools/**`, a whole member) is a blocking finding unless the PR shows its cost and says why.

When the diff adds tests, read their junit durations. A test that runs long because it waits on a
real clock (a sleep, a backoff, a poll interval, a timeout it expects to fire) is a blocking
finding: inject the clock. A bounded window where absence is the assertion is the exception
(`docs/canonical/seam-fidelity.md`). Serializing a lane or retrying a suite to hide one flaky test is a
blocking finding: quarantine that test with a ticket and an expiry.

### L9 — Test efficiency

*Does every changed test, fixture, harness and row run in parallel and set up only once?*

Apply the audit table in `docs/canonical/test-efficiency.md` § Efficiency audit to every test file,
fixture, provisioning script, bucket and CI row the PR adds or changes. Inside `data/**`, also
apply `data/docs/CONVENTIONS.md` § Tests run in parallel and set up only what they read. These are
blocking findings:

- a file that reads rows, roles, rulings or files another file seeded, or a shared identity
  constant two files write;
- a hard-coded pytest `-n`, or a suite serialized to hide one test;
- a fixture that replays the migration chain when its subject is not migration history;
- deterministic expensive setup (enumeration, parsing, collection, compilation) rebuilt per test;
- a cache keyed by a name, path, branch or mtime instead of the sha256 of its complete inputs, or
  one that reads a mismatch as a hit;
- an unbounded retry, or one with no backoff, against a remote limit;
- a new script, step or job for a proof that fits an existing bucket;
- a new bucket, shard, lane or matrix row whose PR does not state its parallelism, measured wall
  time and budget.

Ask for per-test timings when the PR body lacks them. A changed test over 0.5s (unit) or
2s (seam) with no stated reason, or a database seam file over 60s in a loadfile bucket, is a P2.

## Delegating the lenses

Lens work is parallel and bounded, so it delegates well — but **you** scope the diff, read the
spec, and adjudicate. A lane never decides the verdict.

Route by what the lens actually needs:

- **L1, L2, L3, L6, L7, L8, L9** are mechanical and externally verifiable — grep, trace, run a gate, diff a
  generated file. Give them the cheapest capable lane.
- **L4** is judgment: was this the right way, in the spirit of the spec, the simplest thing that
  could work? Give it a high-judgment lane, and give it the spec, not a summary of the spec.
- **L5** is taste. Prefer a Claude lane; frontend structure especially.

Split a lens into more than one lane when the diff spans surfaces — L1 across a Python producer
and a TS consumer is two briefs, not one. More lenses beat more tokens on one lens.

**Execution depends on what's installed on this machine, and degrades cleanly:**

1. `async-subagents` present → its `reviewer` role for L1/L2/L3/L6/L7/L8/L9 (Codex/Sol lanes: fast,
   cheap, good at mechanical verification), native `Agent` subagents for L4/L5. One brief per
   lens, each carrying: the base SHA, the changed-file list, the lens's question, the report
   format below, and an explicit *do not widen beyond this lens*.
2. Subagents but no `async-subagents` → native `Agent` lanes for every lens.
3. Neither → run the lenses inline, in order L1 → L9, cheapest first. The lenses are the
   deliverable; the fan-out is an optimization.

**Judge a lane by its findings, never by its prose.** Delegated review reads polished regardless
of depth. Parse the `SEVERITY` lines and the evidence; discard the narration.

## Verify each finding before you report it

Every finding must survive this before it reaches the author:

```bash
git diff "$BASE"...HEAD -- <the file you are blaming>
```

**Read the hunk.** A review that blamed a scope resolver for weakening a refusal was wrong — the
PR's only change in that region was a comment, and trunk had behaved that way for months. The
"fix" was a regression that CI caught as three failing seams. The claim must be *this PR changed
this behavior*, and the diff is the only thing that establishes it.

Then: is it reachable? Name the caller and the input. A defect no supported path can reach is a
note, not a blocker.

If a finding turns out to be wrong after you have reported it, say so plainly and record why the
original behavior was right — that reasoning is usually the durable part.

## Report format

Group by severity, most severe first. One block per finding:

```
### <one-line statement of the defect>
SEVERITY: P0 | P1 | P2 | P3
FILE: <path>:<line>
CLAIM: <the contract or invariant violated, in one sentence>
FAILURE: <concrete inputs or state -> wrong output, with both values>
EVIDENCE: <file:line citations, diff hunks, command output — enough to re-derive without you>
FIX: <the smallest remediation boundary, and where it belongs>
```

P0/P1 block the merge. P2/P3 are recorded separately so they cannot be mistaken for merge
requirements. Close with:

- **Validation** — exact commands run and their results, in a table. Name every residual
  evidence gap: a gate you could not run is a gap, not a pass.
- **Verdict** — `PASS`, `NEEDS_WORK`, or `NEEDS_DECISION` (contradictory requirements or an
  ownership question the reviewer must not resolve alone). `PASS` means safe and conformant to
  merge, not theoretically perfect.

Say plainly when there are no blocking findings. Do not manufacture P2s to look thorough.

## What happens after the report

Default: report, and stop. Pushing to a branch and posting to a PR are outward-facing and need
explicit authorization each time — approval on one PR does not carry to the next.

When authorized to repair, the repo's own convention applies: fix on the branch, then post one
note saying what changed and why, with the red-verified evidence for each fix and an explicit
"revert either if you'd rather take a different approach." A PR is not merge-ready with an
unresolved review thread — each is closed by a fix with evidence, or by a reply citing
`file:line`.

Every comment you post — the note, a review submission body, an inline comment, a reply on a
thread — starts with the agent watermark: `[AGENT]`, or `[AGENT model=<model-id>]` when you know
your model. `docs/development.md` § "Watermark every agent comment on GitHub and Linear" is the
rule. It covers Linear issue comments too. A PR you open carries no watermark.


## Auditing an existing suite you do not trust

L1 to L3 review a diff. This audits code already written, when a green suite does not
convince you — "passes in tests, fails live." Read `docs/canonical/seam-fidelity.md` first.

### Workflow

1. **Inventory.** Grep the suite for faking idioms (`mock`, `Fake`,
   `monkeypatch`, `scripted`, `ScriptedModel`, `InMemory`, `stub`) and for live
   lanes (`live`, `skipif`, `RUN_LIVE`, `LIVE_LLM`, `emulator`).
2. **Classify each fake by seam** using the doctrine's table: FAITHFUL (wire-fake,
   emulator, real+constraints) vs LYING (decision-seam, in-memory-dict).
3. **Flag** rubber-stamp golden/parity fixtures (regenerated with the code) and
   opt-in/skipped or mis-scoped live lanes — e.g. a "live" lane that forbids the
   real model or only checks token counts.
4. **Find the cross-repo seam** — does any test drive the real upstream runtime,
   or does every repo mock its dependencies?
5. **Recommend the move** for each: which true boundary to cut at, and the bug
   class it would then catch.

### Output

A findings table — `file · current seam · faithful seam · bug class it would
catch` — plus a prioritized remediation list.

If the repository has **no** faithful seam for a dependency, stop.
Require `docs/canonical/seam-fidelity.md` § Building a seam before more audit.
Offer to update the member test-fidelity charter with the findings.

## Auditing a suite for cost

When a suite is slow rather than untrustworthy, run `docs/canonical/test-efficiency.md`
§ Efficiency audit over the whole suite, beside a load-sensitive shape pass
(`tools/ci/gate/test_shape_gate.py`). Rank JUnit or `--durations=0` output by setup plus call,
take the top twenty, and report `file · cost · cause · fix · saving`, marking each saving as
measured or estimated. Never cut a fault, node or proof to buy time; that is an L3 finding.
